text:
maria: Hey — quick FYI found while reviewing the TypeScript SDK vs REST contract for the generate endpoint. Behavior mismatch on boolean flags and empty-list serialization.

sam: ah — do you have a minimal repro?

maria: Yep. On REST we treat omitted fields as unset, but the TS SDK appears to always send `max_tokens` and `stop` even when undefined which changes model routing. Example: REST request (no stop key) yields different tokenization path.

maria: curl example:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","prompt":"hi"}'
```
This arrives server-side with no `stop` field.

maria: TS SDK does: 
```ts
client.generate({ model: 'rwd-7b', prompt: 'hi', stop: undefined })
```
and the JSON ends up with "stop": null (or `[]` in other cases).

lia: Interesting. Our Python SDK (py-sdk) omits keys for None by default, so REST sees them as absent. We need to sync defaults and serialization behavior.

kevin: Is the concrete issue that server interprets `stop: []` as an explicit empty stop set vs missing means fallback to model-default stops?

maria: Exactly. That causes small but observable differences in generation, esp. for legacy models. Also boolean flags like `verbose` — TS sends `verbose: false` which the server interprets as present and disables a fallback; py omits it and server falls back to a config.

sam: Any proposal? Options: 1) make TS SDK drop undefined/null keys (like py) 2) make server treat explicit null/empty same as absent 3) document differences and make callers explicit.

lia: Leaning 1 or 2. Changing server might be safer in the short-term (idempotent), but SDK change is cleaner.

kevin: We should also add integration tests to catch regressions: a matrix test that compares REST direct call vs py-sdk vs ts-sdk for a small set of params (stop=[], stop omitted, stop=null, verbose omitted, verbose:false).

maria: +1 on tests. I'll open a quick PR to adjust ts-sdk serializer to drop undefined/null. Sam — can you own server-side tolerance (interpret null/empty as absent) as a fallback?

sam: Yep, will add a defensive layer in request parsing so null/[] treated as missing for generation routing. Will ping when deployed.

sdk-ci-bot: CI: ran tests for repo ts-sdk — 1 failing test (serde-omit-undefined) — created issue #412.

maria: Thanks. I'll add the integration matrix and a couple of unit tests for the py-sdk behavior so we can assert parity.

lia: Also note: param naming differences (camelCase vs snake_case) cause confusion in examples. We should normalize in docs and make sure auto-generated REST JSON uses snake_case keys to match backend canonical names.

kevin: Agreed. We should add a lint step in SDK generator to map param aliases.

maria: Cool — action items: maria -> PR to ts-sdk serializer; sam -> server tolerant parsing; lia -> doc update + examples; kevin -> generator lint rule + tests. I'll follow up with PR links. Thanks :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — ping when the server patch is live so I can run the integration matrix.

kevin: fyi I'll add a short runbook note to eng-platform about this class of bug (serialization vs omit) so on-call knows common symptoms.

maria: neat. Closing loop later today.
